<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

Two published vibrational assignment sheets for a microcrystalline Fe(II) spin-crossover complex disagree about which bands in the 150-2200 cm-1 window mark the low-spin and high-spin states, and each sheet reproduces the spectra at the single temperature it was written for. Under /app you will find spectra/ with variable-temperature Raman at 532, 785 and 1064 nm and IR spectra at 300, 200, 150 and 100 K, each a two-column CSV of wavenumber_cm1 and intensity on a 1 cm-1 grid; sheets/sheet_A.csv and sheets/sheet_B.csv with columns band_id, center_cm1, mode_label and marker; bands.csv, the consolidated 18-band list your audit must cover; susceptibility.csv with T_K, chi_M_T_cm3Kmol and gamma_HS, the susceptibility-derived total high-spin fraction; and README.md describing the formats. No report exists yet.

Write one JSON audit to /app/report.json. It must be an object with state_fractions, mapping the four temperature strings "100", "150", "200" and "300" to the overall high-spin fraction; ls_breathing_mode_band_id, naming the single band that carries the totally symmetric Fe-N breathing mode; marker_sets, an object holding the "LS" and "HS" band-id arrays, each of which must be exactly the band ids you assign to that state and must not be empty; unresolvable_bands, listing the band ids the supplied data cannot settle; and bands, holding exactly one entry for every band id in /app/bands.csv and no id outside it. Each entry in bands gives band_id, center_cm1 (the tabulated centre for that band id in /app/bands.csv, reproduced as given), a single state from "LS", "HS", "BOTH" or "UNRESOLVABLE", ls_phase_activity from "raman", "ir", "both", "neither" or "not_applicable", and implied_hs_fraction keyed by those same four temperature strings, null for a band you call BOTH or UNRESOLVABLE. Every band id in bands.csv must appear exactly once, no id outside it may appear, and the bands you mark UNRESOLVABLE must be exactly the ids listed in unresolvable_bands, so any band you mark UNRESOLVABLE is listed there and any id listed there carries the UNRESOLVABLE state.

For every band you call LS or HS, the high-spin fraction implied by that band's own integrated intensity must be non-decreasing as the temperature rises from 100 to 300 K and stay within 0.10 of the susceptibility-derived fraction at each of those four temperatures, and the band's placement must be supported by the 532 nm and the 785 nm Raman data alike; the top-level state_fractions must stay within 0.05 of the susceptibility values. The low-spin phase is centrosymmetric, so state every band's activity in that phase - the intrinsic activity of the band's own pure low-spin component - as "raman", "ir", "both" or "neither", where mutual exclusion means no band is active in both Raman and IR in that phase and "not_applicable" is reserved for a band whose low-spin-phase activity the data leave undetermined; name as the breathing-mode carrier a low-spin band that is Raman-active and IR-inactive in that phase and whose implied fraction follows the low-spin fraction to within 0.10 of the susceptibility-derived values at each temperature.

You have 14400 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.

I’ll read the spectra, assignment sheets, and susceptibility data, then compare integrated band intensities across temperatures. The main check is whether each proposed state marker tracks the susceptibility fractions in both 532 and 785 nm Raman data.

const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python - <<'PY'
import numpy as np, csv,glob,os
bands=[233,257,418,447,507,534,566,762,784,1012,1291,1312,1472,1501,1601,2052,2076,2140]
for pref in ['raman_532nm','raman_785nm','ir']:
 fs=glob.glob('/app/spectra/'+pref+'*')
 fs.sort()
 for f in [fs[0],fs[-1]]:
  y=np.array([float(r['intensity']) for r in csv.DictReader(open(f))]); x=np.arange(150,2201)
  print('\n',os.path.basename(f))
  for b in bands:
   m=(x>=b-8)&(x<=b+8)
   i=np.where(m)[0][np.argmax(y[m])]
   print(b,round(x[i],1),round(y[i],2),end='; ')
  print()
PY",workdir:"/app",max_output_tokens:4000}); text(r.output);

import csv, numpy as np, glob, os
from scipy.stats import linregress
bands=[233,257,418,447,507,534,566,762,784,1012,1291,1312,1472,1501,1601,2052,2076,2140]
Ts=[100,150,200,300]; gam=np.array([.06,.26,.55,.84])
for mod in ['raman_532nm','raman_785nm','raman_1064nm','ir']:
 print('\n',mod)
 vals=[]
 for T in Ts:
  data=np.loadtxt(f'/app/spectra/{mod}_{T}K.csv' if mod=='ir' else f'/app/spectra/{mod}_{T}K.csv',delimiter=',',skiprows=1)
  x=data[:,0];y=data[:,1]; ar=[]
  for i,c in enumerate(bands):
   lo=c-11;hi=c+11
   ix=(x>=lo)&(x<=hi)
   # baseline line anchored on mean strips 15-11 cm beyond interval
   l=(x>=lo-5)&(x<lo); r=(x>hi)&(x<=hi+5)
   b0=np.mean(y[l]); b1=np.mean(y[r]); baseline=b0+(b1-b0)*(x[ix]-lo)/(hi-lo)
   area=np.trapezoid(y[ix]-baseline,x[ix])
   ar.append(area)
  vals.append(ar)
 vals=np.array(vals)
 for i,c in enumerate(bands):
  y=vals[:,i]
  lr=linregress(gam,y)
  rr=linregress(1-gam,y)
  # normalize endpoint linear interp predicted gamma from intensities: slope relation, R2 via fits
  print(f'{c}:',np.round(y,1).tolist(), 'R2HS',round(lr.rvalue**2,2),'R2LS',round(rr.rvalue**2,2),'slope',round(lr.slope,1))

const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/regress.py <<'PY'
import numpy as np, os
from scipy.signal import find_peaks, savgol_filter
Ts=[100,150,200,300]; g=np.array([.06,.26,.55,.84]); bands=np.array([233,257,418,447,507,534,566,762,784,1012,1291,1312,1472,1501,1601,2052,2076,2140])
for mod in ['raman_532nm','raman_785nm','raman_1064nm','ir']:
 ys=[]
 for T in Ts:
  d=np.loadtxt(f'/app/spectra/{mod}_{T}K.csv',delimiter=',',skiprows=1); ys.append(d[:,1])
 ys=np.array(ys); x=d[:,0]
 # linear regression against gamma
 X=np.c_[np.ones(4),g]; beta=np.linalg.lstsq(X,ys,rcond=None)[0]
 ls=beta[0]; hs=beta[0]+beta[1]
 print('\n',mod)
 for label,z in [('LS',ls),('HS',hs)]:
  zs=savgol_filter(z,9,2); pk,_=find_peaks(zs,prominence=1,distance=8)
  # around band id find highest positive local peak, report top values by ±15
  print(label,[(int(x[i]),round(zs[i],1)) for i in pk if any(abs(x[i]-c)<=18 for c in bands)])
 for b in bands:
  win=np.abs(x-b)<=12
  l=float(np.max(ls[win])); h=float(np.max(hs[win]));
  # local peak locations
  il=np.where(win)[0][np.argmax(ls[win])]; ih=np.where(win)[0][np.argmax(hs[win])]
  print(f'{b}: LS {x[il]:.0f}:{l:.1f} HS {x[ih]:.0f}:{h:.1f} ratio {h/l if l>0 else 99:.2f}')
PY
